abstract: Let $\Gamma\subset\mathrm{O}^+(n,2)$ be a rational arithmetic group with $n\geq 3$. A non-constant modular form for $\Gamma$ is called strongly reflective if its zero divisor is a reduced union of mirrors of reflections in $\Gamma$. We show that, up to conjugation and multiplication by a nonzero scalar, there are only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms. As a consequence, we establish the finiteness of holomorphic automorphic products of singular weight. These results answer a question posed by Borcherds in 1995 and settle a conjecture of Gritsenko--Nikulin from 1998. As an application, up to conjugation, we prove the finiteness of $\Gamma$ whose corresponding algebra of modular forms is freely generated. The key ingredient is a uniform upper bound on the covolume of $\Gamma$, obtained by adapting the higher-rank lattice convergence theorem of Ab\'ert et al. to the study of the degrees of reflective branch divisors.
hook: Only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms exist, settling a 1995 question of Borcherds.
summary: Strongly reflective modular forms vanish exactly on mirrors of reflections in an arithmetic group. The authors prove there are finitely many up to conjugation, which settles a 1995 question of Borcherds and a 1998 conjecture of Gritsenko and Nikulin. It follows that only finitely many such groups have freely generated algebras of modular forms. The key is a uniform bound on the covolume of the group.
title: Finiteness of strongly reflective modular forms
